Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the year-end RBC calculation for every licensed writing company; component build delegated to the Capital Model Actuary, formula and reserve-driven components certified by the Chief Actuary

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alabama's adoption of the NAIC RBC for Insurers Model Act (312) read against the current-year NAIC Risk-Based Capital Forecasting & Instructions (Life LR001–LR033, P&C PR001 onward, Health XR001 onward); the 51-jurisdiction citation matrix and the factor tables are re-verified every January when the Capital Adequacy (E) Task Force publishes year-end instruction and factor changes

In-scope processes.value: Statutory year-end close → asset and liability data extract → RBC component build (C-0/C-1cs/C-1o/C-2/C-3a/C-3b/C-3c/C-4a/C-4b for life; R0–R5 plus Rcat for P&C; H0–H4 for health) → covariance adjustment → Authorized Control Level and Total Adjusted Capital, run as a forecast at Q1–Q3 and as the filed calculation at year-end, for every entity licensed across the 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: The NAIC RBC blank inside the statutory reporting suite, fed by annual statement Schedule D / Schedule BA / Schedule DB asset detail and Schedule P triangles; component workings held in the actuarial modeling platform and locked to the filed run

Compliance procedure documented.value: RBC Calculation Procedure — per-page data sourcing map, factor table version control, affiliate look-through for C-0/R0, the covariance square-root formula, the Total Adjusted Capital build-up (capital and surplus + AVR + half the apportioned policyholder dividend liability), and the four-eyes recomputation before any number leaves Capital Management

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Actuary; re-approved each January against the NAIC year-end RBC instruction changes and any adopted factor revisions, with the approval memo dated before the first component is built

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Year-end RBC must be complete, tied out and locked by the February statutory close lock so the report can file by March 1; each quarterly forecast run closes 20 business days after quarter-end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Capital close calendar alerts at Jan 15 (current-year factor tables loaded), Feb 1 (draft ACL circulated), Feb 15 (four-eyes recomputation signed) and Feb 25 (calculation locked for the March 1 filing), each addressed to the named component owner

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Locked RBC workbook per company per year, the page-by-page tie-out to the annual statement, the factor table version stamp, reviewer sign-offs and the model change log, retained 7 years (10 where the domiciliary state's record rule is longer) in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any restatement of a filed ACL or Total Adjusted Capital, any unreconciled page tie-out over $250K, and any use of a superseded factor table is logged with root cause, the corrected-filing date and the notification made to the domiciliary analyst

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Actuary signs every recomputation, factor correction and restated RBC ratio before an amended RBC report is re-filed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every licensed writing company's RBC calculation for the reporting year — the filed year-end run plus the three quarterly forecast runs — at the level of each RBC blank line carrying a non-zero amount

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on formula and factor errors; any line that fails to tie to the annual statement by more than $100K or 0.5% of the page total is a fail, as is any restatement of ACL or TAC; two or more fails escalate to the CFO and the Audit Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual (March 1) with quarterly forecasting; the full test runs once a year over the filed year-end calculation, with an abbreviated re-performance of the Q3 forecast to catch factor and mapping drift before year-end

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Capital Management and must not have built, reviewed or signed any RBC component in the year under test

Evidence location for test results.value: RBC calculation test workpaper (line population, tie-out schedule, re-performed covariance, factor version check, exception log) filed in the compliance evidence repository under Capital/RBC/<reporting year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filed RBC blank, the page-to-annual-statement tie-out, the factor table version stamp and the reviewer sign-offs, producible to a financial examiner within 10 business days in the format expected under the NAIC Financial Condition Examiners Handbook capital adequacy procedures

Regulator response path.value: The Statutory Reporting Manager answers domiciliary and lead-state financial analyst questions on the calculation; Regulatory Counsel clears any restatement disclosure before it is sent, and all RBC results are handled as confidential under the Model Act's confidentiality and prohibition-on-advertising sections

checklist.step: Lock the year-end statutory data feed that the RBC calculation will run on
actions: In the statutory reporting suite open Annual Statement ▸ <writing company> ▸ Year-End and set the close status to 'Locked for RBC' once the Controller confirms the last statutory journal has posted.

Export the RBC source set: Schedule D Part 1 (bonds with NAIC designation and sub-designation), Schedule D Parts 2/6 (equities and affiliates), Schedule BA (other long-term invested assets), Schedule DB (derivatives), Schedule F Parts 3/5 (reinsurance recoverable and provision), Schedule P Parts 1–4 (P&C reserve and premium triangles), Exhibits 5–8 (life reserves) and the Five-Year Historical page.
Record the extract timestamp, statement version and surplus figure on the RBC control sheet and email it to the Head of Capital Management as the single agreed starting point.
Freeze the feed: any post-lock statutory adjustment must be raised as a numbered close adjustment and re-run, never edited into the RBC workbook.
checklist.done: the RBC control sheet names one locked statement version, one extract timestamp and one surplus figure that every component owner will build from.

checklist.step: Load the current-year NAIC RBC blank and factor tables and record the version
actions: Download the current-year NAIC Risk-Based Capital Forecasting & Instructions and the RBC blank for the correct formula (Life LR pages, P&C PR pages, Health XR pages) for each writing company's statement type.

Read the 'Changes from Prior Year' section of the instructions and list every factor, line and structural change on the RBC change log — bond designation granularity, real estate factors, longevity and Rcat treatment are the usual movers.
Load the factor tables into the calculation workbook and stamp the workbook header with the instruction year, the factor table release date and the loader's name.
Ask the Chief Actuary to confirm in writing that the loaded formula variant matches the entity's licence type before any component is built.
checklist.done: the workbook carries a stamped instruction-year and factor-release version, and the change log lists every year-on-year formula change with its affected page.

checklist.step: Build the affiliate charge (C-0 for life, R0 for P&C) with full look-through
actions: Pull the affiliate inventory from Schedule D Part 6 Section 1 and reconcile it to the holding company organisational chart maintained by the Corporate Secretary for the Form B registration.
Classify each affiliate as insurance subsidiary subject to RBC, non-insurance subsidiary, investment subsidiary or alien insurer, and apply the instruction's charge for that class.
For each insurance subsidiary obtain that entity's own filed ACL RBC from its Capital Management contact and carry the pro-rata ownership share into C-0/R0 rather than applying a flat asset factor.
Document any indirect or off-balance-sheet guarantee to an affiliate and add the required charge, citing the instruction line.
Post the completed affiliate schedule to the RBC folder with the ownership percentages tied to the Form B.
checklist.done: every affiliate on Schedule D Part 6 appears on the C-0/R0 schedule with a class, an ownership percentage tied to the Form B chart and a charge traceable to a named instruction line.

checklist.step: Build the asset risk components from the investment schedules
actions: Extract the year-end holdings file from the investment book of record by CUSIP, asset class, NAIC designation and sub-designation, book/adjusted carrying value and maturity.
Reconcile the extract total to Schedule D Part 1 and Schedule BA book value; investigate any difference over $50K with the Controller before applying a single factor.

Apply the current-year bond factors by NAIC designation category, the common and preferred stock factors, the mortgage loan factors by category, the real estate factors and the Schedule BA factors to produce C-1o and C-1cs (life) or R1 and R2 (P&C).
Apply the asset concentration adjustment: identify the ten largest issuer exposures across all asset types and double the factor on the qualifying amounts per the instructions.
Hand the priced, designated holdings file plus the concentration schedule to the Capital Model Actuary and keep the Aladdin query definition with it so the extract is reproducible.
checklist.done: asset charges are computed off a holdings file reconciled to Schedule D and Schedule BA, with the ten-largest-issuer concentration adjustment applied and the query definition retained.

checklist.step: Build the credit risk charge on reinsurance recoverables and receivables
actions: Extract the recoverable balance by reinsurer from the ceded administration system: paid recoverable, case and IBNR recoverable, unearned premium ceded and funds held.

Reconcile the extract to Schedule F Part 3 by reinsurer NAIC/AIIN code and to the Schedule F Part 5 provision for reinsurance; differences over $25K go back to the Reinsurance Accountant before factors are applied.

Tag each reinsurer authorised, certified, reciprocal-jurisdiction or unauthorised, and net collateral (letters of credit, trust balances, funds held) against the balance exactly as the RBC instruction permits.
Apply the recoverable credit factor to the uncollateralised net balance and add the receivable-related charges to produce R3 (P&C) or the C-3c/credit element (life).
File the reinsurer-level schedule showing balance, collateral, authorisation status and charge so an examiner can walk one reinsurer end to end.
checklist.done: the credit charge is built from a reinsurer-level schedule reconciled to Schedule F Part 3 with collateral and authorisation status evidenced per reinsurer.

checklist.step: Build the underwriting components from the reserve and premium data
actions: For P&C, extract net loss and LAE reserves and net written premium by RBC line of business exactly as mapped to Schedule P Parts 1–4, and compute the company's own ten-year adverse development experience factor where the instructions permit its use.

Apply the current-year industry reserve risk and premium risk factors line by line, then apply the loss-sensitive contract discount and the line-of-business diversification adjustment to produce R4 and R5.

For life and health, pull net amount at risk by product from the valuation system and apply the C-2 mortality, morbidity and lapse factors by band; for health, build H2 from earned premium by managed-care category and apply the managed care credit.
Reconcile the line-of-business premium and reserve totals back to the annual statement Underwriting and Investment Exhibit or Exhibit 5 before signing the component off.
Send the completed component and its reconciliation to the Capital Model Actuary with the Reserving Actuary's name and date on it.
checklist.done: the underwriting components tie line by line to Schedule P or Exhibit 5, with company-experience and diversification adjustments evidenced and signed by the Reserving Actuary.

checklist.step: Build the interest rate and market risk components from ALM output
actions: Segment the in-force liability into the RBC withdrawal-risk categories (low risk, medium risk, high risk / no surrender charge) using the surrender charge and market-value-adjustment terms held in the policy administration extract.

Apply the C-3a interest rate factors by category, then run the C-3 Phase I cash flow scenarios where the entity exceeds the exemption test, and the C-3 Phase II stochastic scenario set for variable annuity and guaranteed benefit business.
Compute the C-3b health credit risk element and the C-3c market risk element for separate account and guaranteed products, documenting the model point set and the scenario file name used.
Have the Valuation Actuary confirm the liability segmentation agrees with the reserves reported in Exhibit 5 before the charge is released.
Save the run outputs, scenario file and model version into the model governance repository against the year-end run id.
checklist.done: the interest rate and market risk charges are produced from a named, archived model run whose liability segmentation the Valuation Actuary has confirmed against Exhibit 5.

checklist.step: Build the catastrophe risk charge from modelled net PML
actions: Run the year-end exposure set through the licensed hurricane and earthquake models on the version the RBC instructions accept, and pull the gross occurrence exceedance probability curve.

Apply the in-force reinsurance programme structure held by the Reinsurance Manager to produce net occurrence PML at the return periods the instructions specify, and record the reinstatement premium treatment.
Enter the net modelled losses into the Rcat pages (earthquake and hurricane components) and apply the contingent credit risk charge on the reinsurance recoveries assumed in the net figures.
Reconcile the modelled exposure in-force to the policy administration in-force count and total insured value; explain any variance over 2% in the run memo.
File the model run id, model version, event set and net PML table alongside the Rcat pages.
checklist.done: Rcat is populated from a named, reproducible model run whose exposure ties to policy administration in-force and whose net PML reflects the actual reinsurance structure.

checklist.step: Build the business risk component and any remaining charges
actions: For life, compute C-4a from premium income and separate account liabilities per the instruction factors, and C-4b from the health administrative expense base.

Pull the guaranty fund assessment history, long-term care and disability blocks, and any excessive-growth trigger data that drive additional charges, and confirm each against the annual statement page it comes from.
Add off-balance-sheet and other items — non-controlled assets, guarantees for affiliates, contingent liabilities disclosed in the Notes to Financial Statements — to the relevant RBC line.
Circulate the completed component to the Controller for confirmation that nothing disclosed in the Notes has been omitted from the charge.
checklist.done: the business risk and off-balance-sheet charges are complete, each tied to a named annual statement page or note, with Controller confirmation of completeness.

checklist.step: Apply the covariance adjustment and compute Authorized Control Level RBC
actions: Assemble the component totals onto the RBC calculation page and check each one against the signed component hand-off from its owner.

Apply the formula's covariance treatment exactly as instructed — for P&C, ACL = R0 + the square root of the sum of squares of R1 through R5 plus Rcat; for life, apply the prescribed square-root grouping of the C-1o/C-3a and C-1cs/C-3c pairs with C-0 and C-4a outside the radical.
Compute Company Action Level RBC as twice ACL and record ACL, CAL, Regulatory Action Level (150% of ACL), Authorized Control Level (100%) and Mandatory Control Level (70%) on the summary page.
Compare each component and the ACL to the prior year and to the latest quarterly forecast, and write a one-line driver explanation for any movement over 10%.
Protect the formula cells and route the summary to the Head of Capital Management.
checklist.done: ACL is computed with the instructed covariance treatment, the four action level amounts are stated, and every component movement over 10% carries a written driver.

checklist.step: Compute Total Adjusted Capital and the RBC ratio
actions: Start from capital and surplus as reported on the annual statement Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds page for the locked statement version.

Add the Asset Valuation Reserve balance, the prescribed share of the apportioned policyholder dividend liability, and any voluntary investment reserves the instructions allow, itemising each adjustment with its statement line reference.
Deduct the items the instructions require, including the RBC share of subsidiary capital already counted through C-0/R0, so no dollar of capital is counted twice.
Compute the RBC ratio as Total Adjusted Capital divided by Authorized Control Level RBC, expressed to one decimal place, and state the dollar headroom to the Company Action Level trigger.
Sign the TAC build-up schedule and file it with the calculation.
checklist.done: a signed TAC build-up ties to the reported surplus line with every adjustment itemised, and the RBC ratio and dollar headroom to Company Action Level are stated.

checklist.step: Tie every RBC page back to the annual statement source page
actions: Run the statutory reporting suite's RBC cross-check report, which compares RBC input lines to their annual statement source pages, and export the exception list.

For each cross-check exception, open the RBC page and the cited statement page side by side, identify whether the cause is a mapping error, a timing difference or a genuine data error, and record the answer on the tie-out schedule.
Clear every difference over $100K or 0.5% of the page total; anything left unresolved is written up as an exception with an owner rather than overridden.
Confirm the Five-Year Historical page RBC lines agree with the current-year ACL and TAC before the statement is finalised.
checklist.done: the cross-check exception list is cleared to zero or every residual is written up with a cause and an owner on the tie-out schedule.

checklist.step: Have the calculation independently recomputed under model governance
actions: Register the RBC calculation as a tier-1 model in the model governance repository with the current-year version, owner and validation date.

Independently rebuild at least the covariance calculation, the ten largest asset factor applications and the TAC build-up from the locked source extract, without opening the production workbook first.
Compare the independent result to the production result line by line and require a written explanation for any difference above $50K.
Confirm the factor table version stamped on the workbook matches the NAIC release for the reporting year, and that the change log records every year-on-year formula change.
Issue the validation memo with findings, severity and due dates, and attach it to the model record.
checklist.done: a dated validation memo shows an independent rebuild agreeing to the production calculation, with every difference above $50K explained and the factor version confirmed.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly RBC forecast so year-end holds no surprises
actions: Within 20 business days of each quarter-end, roll the components forward using the quarterly statement balance sheet, the quarter's premium and reserve movement and the current holdings file.
Project ACL and TAC to 31 December using the business plan volumes, the planned dividend and any planned capital action supplied by the Treasury Manager.
Publish the forecast RBC ratio, the projected headroom to Company Action Level and the three largest drivers of movement to the CFO and the Chief Risk Officer.
Where the forecast ratio falls below the board's internal operating threshold, raise it into the capital escalation process the same week rather than waiting for year-end.
checklist.done: each quarter closes with a published forecast ACL, TAC, ratio and headroom, and any breach of the internal operating threshold has already been escalated.

checklist.step: Lock, sign and archive the filed calculation
actions: Confirm every component carries its owner's signed hand-off and that the model validation memo has no open high-severity finding.
Lock the workbook, generate the final RBC pages and hand the package to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for the March 1 filing with the calculation date and version noted on the transmittal.

Deposit the locked workbook, source extracts, factor table version, tie-out schedule, validation memo and sign-offs into the compliance evidence repository under Capital/RBC/<reporting year> with the 7-year retention label applied.
Confirm the repository index makes the record retrievable by writing company, NAIC company code and reporting year.
checklist.done: the locked, signed calculation package is archived under a 7-year retention label and retrievable by company code and reporting year.

testing.step: Build the population of RBC lines subject to test
actions: Export every RBC blank line with a non-zero amount for each licensed writing company from the filed year-end run, plus the three quarterly forecast runs, tagged by page, component and owner.
Add the component hand-off register so a component that was built but never carried into the summary cannot hide.
Reconcile the population's ACL and TAC totals to the RBC report as filed with the domiciliary department and resolve any difference before drawing a sample.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the filed ACL and TAC for every writing company and is signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the RBC inputs to the annual statement as source of record
actions: Match each populated RBC input line to its cited annual statement page — Schedule D Part 1, Schedule BA, Schedule F Part 3, Schedule P Parts 1–4, Exhibit 5 — and compute the difference.
List every difference above $100K or 0.5% of the page total as an automatic exception regardless of the explanation offered.

Confirm the statement version used by Capital Management is the version actually filed, by comparing the surplus figure on the RBC control sheet to the filed Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds page.
Confirm the Five-Year Historical page RBC lines agree with the filed ACL and TAC.
testing.done: every RBC input traces to the filed annual statement page within threshold, or the difference is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document a reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of the components that individually exceed 10% of pre-covariance RBC, and 100% of any component restated or corrected during the year.
Take 25 further lines at random using a recorded seed, stratified so each RBC page is represented, with a minimum sample of 40 lines overall.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add every line the prior year's test raised as an exception as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible from the recorded seed, covers all components above 10% of pre-covariance RBC and includes every prior-year exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the asset risk factor application on the sample
actions: Open the current-year NAIC RBC instructions to the sampled asset page and read the factor for each NAIC designation, mortgage category and Schedule BA class without looking at the production workbook first.
Recompute the charge from the holdings file for the sampled lines and compare to the recorded charge; a right answer reached with a prior-year factor is still an exception.
Re-derive the ten largest issuer exposures independently and confirm the concentration adjustment doubled the factor on the correct amounts.
Screenshot the instruction page relied on into the workpaper next to the recomputation.
testing.done: each sampled asset line has an independent recomputation, a captured instruction page and a stated agree/disagree conclusion.

testing.step: Re-perform the underwriting components from the statutory schedules
actions: Rebuild net reserves and net written premium by RBC line of business straight from Schedule P Parts 1–4 (or Exhibit 5 for life) and apply the published industry factors.
Recompute the company-experience adverse development factor from the ten-year triangle and confirm the entity qualified to use it under the instruction's test.
Recompute the loss-sensitive discount and the line-of-business diversification adjustment and compare to the filed R4 and R5.
Flag any mapping of a Schedule P line to the wrong RBC line of business as an exception, since it silently changes the factor.
testing.done: R4 and R5 (or C-2) are independently rebuilt from the statutory schedules and either agree with the filed amounts or the mapping or factor difference is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the covariance adjustment, ACL and Total Adjusted Capital
actions: Rebuild the covariance formula from the instruction text in a clean workbook and feed it the filed component totals.

Confirm the correct components sit inside and outside the square root — C-0 and C-4a outside for life, R0 outside for P&C — as an inversion here moves ACL materially without any single component being wrong.
Rebuild the TAC schedule from the filed surplus line, the AVR balance and the apportioned dividend liability, and confirm no subsidiary capital is counted both in TAC and through C-0/R0.
Recompute the RBC ratio to one decimal place and compare to the ratio reported to the board and to the domiciliary department.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt covariance calculation and TAC schedule reproduce the filed ACL, TAC and RBC ratio, or the difference is quantified.

testing.step: Verify factor table version control and model change governance
actions: Compare the factor table version stamped on the filed workbook to the NAIC release for the reporting year and confirm they match exactly.
Read the RBC change log against the 'Changes from Prior Year' section of the instructions and confirm every published change was implemented, not just the ones that reduced the charge.
Confirm the model record shows a validation memo dated before the filing date with no open high-severity finding.
Confirm the workbook's protected formula cells were not unlocked between the validation date and the filing date, using the repository's version history.
testing.done: the filed workbook uses the correct factor release, implements every published formula change, and was validated and unaltered before filing.

testing.step: Recompute the action level thresholds and the trend test
actions: Recompute Company Action Level as 200% of ACL, Regulatory Action Level as 150%, Authorized Control Level as 100% and Mandatory Control Level as 70%, and compare each to the reported figures.

Recompute the trend test on its own terms — for life, TAC between 200% and 250% of ACL with a negative surplus trend; for P&C, between 200% and 300% with a combined ratio above 120% — and confirm the conclusion recorded matches.
Confirm the dollar headroom to Company Action Level reported to the board equals TAC minus 200% of ACL.
Any threshold or trend test miscalculation is a reportable control failure, not a presentational point, because it determines whether an RBC plan was owed.
testing.done: all four action level amounts and the trend test conclusion are independently recomputed and agree with what was reported to the board and the regulator.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying the writing company, RBC page and line, the dollar effect on ACL or TAC, and the effect on the RBC ratio in basis points.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — stale factor table, source mapping error, unlocked formula, missed instruction change, late statutory adjustment — and name an owner.
Where the aggregate effect would change an action level conclusion, open an amended-RBC assessment with Regulatory Counsel and the Chief Actuary the same week.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest line.
testing.done: every exception carries a dollar and basis-point effect, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance formula and factor threshold and the $100K / 0.5% tie-out threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references that support it and the net effect on the reported RBC ratio.
Have the independent reviewer, who built and reviewed no component in the tested year, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any amended-filing recommendation to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under Capital/RBC/<reporting year>.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Accountable for keeping Total Adjusted Capital above the Company Action Level in every writing company; day-to-day monitoring run by the Capital Management Manager, escalation shared with the Chief Risk Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the action level sections of Alabama's RBC for Insurers Model Act (312) adoption and the 50 parallel adoptions, confirming each state's Company Action Level (200% of ACL), Regulatory Action Level (150%), Authorized Control Level (100%) and Mandatory Control Level (70%) triggers plus the 45-day RBC plan deadline; re-read each January and on any state amendment bulletin

In-scope processes.value: Monthly capital roll-forward and quarterly RBC forecasting for every licensed writing company, the trend test, the internal early-warning ladder above the statutory triggers, dividend and capital extraction approval, and the escalation path from Capital Management to the CFO, the Board Risk Committee and the domiciliary commissioner

In-scope systems.value: Capital forecast and monthly roll-forward models in the planning platform, with the RBC ratio dashboard published to the board portal and breach events raised in the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Capital Monitoring and Escalation Procedure — the internal trigger ladder (green above 400% of ACL, amber 300–400%, red below 300%) sitting above the statutory 200% Company Action Level, the roll-forward method, the named escalation recipients at each rung, and the 45-day RBC plan production timetable

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board Risk Committee on the recommendation of the CFO and Chief Risk Officer; the trigger ladder is re-approved annually with the risk appetite statement and after any material reinsurance, dividend or acquisition decision

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Monthly capital dashboard to the CFO by working day 10; quarterly forecast to the Board Risk Committee; and, on a Company Action Level event, the RBC plan to the domiciliary commissioner within 45 days of the triggering RBC report

Deadline reminders configured.value: Automated alerts on working day 5 for the roll-forward inputs, working day 10 for the dashboard, and an immediate alert to the CFO, Chief Risk Officer and Head of Capital Management the moment a forecast or actual ratio crosses the amber or red rung

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Monthly capital dashboards, roll-forward workings, breach notifications, escalation minutes, Board Risk Committee papers and any RBC plan filed with a commissioner, retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every internal trigger breach and every statutory action level event is raised as a risk event with the date crossed, the driver, the management action taken, the regulator notification made and the date the ratio returned above trigger

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Risk Officer signs off the management action plan behind every amber or red breach and confirms closure only once the ratio has held above the trigger for two consecutive month-ends

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every monthly capital roll-forward and quarterly forecast produced in the year for each writing company, plus every trigger breach event raised in the GRC platform

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missed detection — any month where the ratio crossed a trigger and no alert or escalation was raised is a fail, as is any escalation raised more than 5 business days after the crossing; any Company Action Level event without an RBC plan filed inside 45 days is a reportable breach

Evidence location for test results.value: Capital monitoring test workpaper (month population, recomputed ratios, alert-timing analysis, escalation trace, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Capital/Monitoring/<year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The trigger ladder approval, the twelve monthly dashboards, the breach register and any filed RBC plan, presentable to a domiciliary financial analyst or examination team within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: The CFO leads the response to a Company Action Level event and owns the RBC plan; Regulatory Counsel clears every communication to the commissioner, and no capital or RBC level is ever used in advertising, which the Model Act prohibits

checklist.step: Set the internal trigger ladder above the statutory action levels
actions: Write the four statutory triggers into the risk appetite statement in dollar terms per writing company: Company Action Level at 200% of ACL, Regulatory Action Level at 150%, Authorized Control Level at 100%, Mandatory Control Level at 70%.
Set the internal ladder above them — green above 400% of ACL, amber 300–400%, red below 300% — so management acts long before a statutory trigger is in reach.

Name the recipient and the response time for each rung: amber to the CFO and Head of Capital Management within 2 business days, red to the CFO, CEO and Board Risk Committee chair within 1 business day.
Load the ladder into the GRC platform as a monitored key risk indicator with the thresholds encoded, and take the Board Risk Committee's approval at the annual appetite review.
checklist.done: the appetite statement carries dollar triggers per writing company, a named recipient and response time per rung, encoded as a KRI and approved by the Board Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Roll Total Adjusted Capital forward every month
actions: By working day 5 pull the month-end statutory surplus per writing company from the general ledger, together with the AVR movement and the apportioned dividend liability.

Bridge from prior month: statutory net income, unrealised investment gains and losses, realised impairments, reserve strengthening or release, dividends paid to the holding company and capital contributions received.
Get the Treasury Manager to confirm in writing any intercompany dividend or contribution settled in the month, with the date and the approving state.
Publish the roll-forward with each bridging item named, so a movement in the ratio can always be attributed to a specific line.
checklist.done: each writing company has a month-end TAC figure bridged from the prior month with every movement over $1M named and Treasury confirmation of any capital movement.

checklist.step: Roll the Authorized Control Level requirement forward on the same cycle
actions: Update the asset risk components for the month's holdings file: new purchases, sales, NAIC designation migrations and impairments taken.
Update the underwriting components for the month's written premium and any reserve movement booked by the Reserving Actuary.
Re-apply the covariance formula to the refreshed components to produce a month-end ACL estimate, and flag it clearly as an estimate rather than a filed figure.
Explain any month-on-month ACL movement over 5% in one line, naming the component that caused it.
checklist.done: a month-end ACL estimate exists per writing company with every movement over 5% attributed to a named component.

checklist.step: Compute the ratio, the headroom and the distance to each trigger
actions: Compute the RBC ratio as TAC divided by ACL for every writing company and for the group on a sum-of-parts basis.
State the dollar headroom to each rung: to the internal amber and red triggers, and to the statutory Company Action Level (TAC minus 200% of ACL).
Show the twelve-month trend of the ratio alongside the trigger lines so a slow slide is as visible as a sudden drop.
Publish the dashboard to the CFO, Chief Risk Officer and Head of Capital Management by working day 10 with the three largest movements called out.
checklist.done: the working-day-10 dashboard states the ratio, the dollar headroom to every rung and a twelve-month trend for each writing company.

checklist.step: Run the trend test whenever the ratio approaches the Company Action Level band
actions: Where TAC sits between 200% and 250% of ACL for a life company, apply the trend test the Model Act prescribes and check whether the surplus trend is negative.
Where a P&C company sits between 200% and 300% of ACL, test whether the combined ratio exceeds 120%, which converts the position into a Company Action Level event.
Record the tested inputs — the two prior year-end TAC figures, the combined ratio calculation and its source page — on the trend test sheet.
Report a positive trend test to the CFO and Regulatory Counsel the same day, because it creates the RBC plan obligation exactly as a ratio breach would.
checklist.done: any company inside the trend test band has a dated trend test with its inputs recorded and a stated pass or fail.

checklist.step: Monitor the leading indicators that move capital before the ratio does
actions: Track the NAIC IRIS ratios monthly and flag any ratio outside its usual range, since the domiciliary analyst will see the same signal at year-end.
Track investment watch-list items from the Chief Investment Officer: downgrades below NAIC 3, watch-listed issuers and unrealised loss positions over 20% of book value.
Track reserve early warnings from the Reserving Actuary: any line where the latest indication exceeds the carried reserve by more than 5%.
Track reinsurer credit events from the Reinsurance Credit & Security Analyst, since a downgrade converts collateralised recoverables into a capital charge.
Report the indicator pack alongside the monthly capital dashboard with any indicator that moved into breach highlighted.
checklist.done: the monthly pack carries IRIS ratios, investment watch-list, reserve indications and reinsurer credit events, each with a stated in-range or breach status.

checklist.step: Test dividend and capital extraction capacity before any payment is approved
actions: Before any dividend to the holding company, recompute the post-dividend RBC ratio and the post-dividend headroom to the internal amber trigger.

Apply the domiciliary state's extraordinary dividend test (the greater or lesser of 10% of surplus and prior-year net gain from operations, as that state prescribes) and determine whether prior commissioner approval is required.
Where approval is required, hand Regulatory Counsel the Form B/Form D package and do not settle until the approval or the non-disapproval period has run.
Refuse any extraction that would take the forecast ratio below the amber rung without a written CFO and Chief Risk Officer decision on file.
checklist.done: no dividend settles without a recomputed post-payment ratio, an extraordinary dividend determination and, where needed, a commissioner approval on file.

checklist.step: Raise the breach event the moment a trigger is crossed
actions: Open a risk event in the GRC platform on the day the actual or forecast ratio crosses a rung, recording the writing company, the rung, the ratio, the dollar shortfall and the driver.
Notify the recipients named for that rung inside the response time set in the appetite statement, by email with the dashboard attached.
Never net a breach away with an expected future recovery — the event is raised on the position as it stands at month-end.
Attach the roll-forward and the ACL estimate that produced the crossing so the event is self-supporting.
checklist.done: every crossing has a dated risk event with the ratio, shortfall, driver and evidence attached, notified inside the rung's response time.

checklist.step: Build the management action plan behind the breach
actions: Convene Finance, Actuarial, Investments and Reinsurance within 5 business days of the event and cost each available lever.

Quantify each lever's RBC ratio effect and lead time: quota share or adverse development cover to cut R4/R5 or C-2, de-risking the asset portfolio to cut C-1/R1-R2, a capital contribution from the parent, suspending shareholder dividends, or slowing new business in capital-intensive lines.
Choose the combination that restores the ratio above the trigger and write the sequence, the owner and the date for each action.
Have the Chief Risk Officer approve the plan and load the actions into the GRC event with due dates.
checklist.done: the breach event carries a costed, sequenced action plan with owners, dates, a quantified ratio effect and Chief Risk Officer approval.

checklist.step: Produce the RBC plan within 45 days of a Company Action Level event
actions: On a Company Action Level event — a ratio below 200% of ACL or a failed trend test — start the 45-day clock from the RBC report date and record the due date in the escalation event.

Draft the RBC plan the Model Act requires: the conditions that contributed to the event, the proposed corrective actions, four-year financial projections with and without the corrective actions, the key assumptions behind the projections, and the quality of and problems associated with the insurer's business.
Have the Chief Actuary and the Appointed Actuary confirm the projection assumptions are consistent with the reserving and pricing bases.

Take the plan to the board for adoption, then file it with the domiciliary commissioner inside the 45 days through the channel Regulatory Counsel confirms, and copy every other state that requests it.
checklist.done: a board-adopted RBC plan carrying the five statutory content elements is filed with the domiciliary commissioner inside 45 days of the triggering report.

checklist.step: Escalate to the board and record the decisions
actions: Table the capital position at every Board Risk Committee meeting: ratio by writing company, headroom to each trigger, forecast to year-end and the status of any open action plan.
Where a rung has been crossed, present the event, the driver, the action plan and the expected recovery date as a standing agenda item until it closes.
Ask the Corporate Secretary to minute the committee's decision on each proposed capital action, naming who approved what.
Publish the pack to the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting so directors can challenge the assumptions.
checklist.done: each committee cycle has a capital paper on the portal, minuted decisions on every capital action and a standing item for each open breach.

checklist.step: Track the recovery until the ratio holds above the trigger
actions: Re-measure the ratio at every month-end against the recovery path set in the action plan and report actual versus plan.
Where an action slips its date or delivers less than the quantified effect, re-open the plan rather than extending the date silently.
Keep the risk event open until the ratio has held above the trigger for two consecutive month-ends.
Have the Chief Risk Officer sign the closure note stating the final ratio and the actions that delivered it.
checklist.done: the event closes only on a signed note showing two consecutive month-ends above the trigger and the actions that delivered the recovery.

checklist.step: Handle regulator contact arising from the capital position
actions: Route every domiciliary or lead-state analyst question about capital adequacy through a single log with the date received, the question and the due date.
Draft the response with Capital Management, confirming each figure against the filed RBC report before it is sent.
Confirm no RBC level or ratio appears in any advertisement, sales material or public statement, which the Model Act's prohibition section forbids, and take down anything that does.
File the question, the response and the supporting figures in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every regulator question on capital has a logged, figure-verified response on file, and no RBC level appears in any public material.

checklist.step: Refresh the monitoring inputs when the business changes materially
actions: Re-run the trigger ladder in dollar terms after any acquisition, new state licence, large reinsurance restructuring or reserve strengthening, since the same percentage rung is now a different dollar amount.
Re-point the roll-forward to any newly licensed writing company within one month of licensure so it is never monitored outside the framework.
Ask Capital Management to re-baseline the forecast to the revised business plan and re-publish the headroom figures.
Take material changes back to the Board Risk Committee for re-approval rather than absorbing them into the existing ladder.
checklist.done: the ladder, roll-forward scope and forecast baseline are refreshed and re-approved after every material change, with no licensed entity outside the framework.

checklist.step: Archive the monitoring record for the retention period
actions: File each month's dashboard, roll-forward, ACL estimate and indicator pack under Capital/Monitoring/<year>/<month>.
File every breach event, action plan, closure note, board paper and filed RBC plan under the same tree with the event id.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm the index makes records retrievable by writing company, month and trigger rung.
Reconcile the count of archived months to twelve per writing company before the year closes.
checklist.done: twelve monitoring records per writing company plus every breach and board paper are archived under a 7-year label and retrievable by company and month.

testing.step: Build the population of monitoring cycles and breach events
actions: List every writing company licensed at any point in the year and expand to one row per company per month, so a company licensed mid-year still has rows from its licence date.
Match each row to an archived dashboard, roll-forward and ACL estimate; missing months are automatic exceptions before any judgement is applied.
Extract every capital risk event raised in the GRC platform in the year with its rung, crossing date and closure date.
testing.done: the population covers every licensed company-month with its monitoring artefacts matched, and every GRC capital event is captured.

testing.step: Reconcile the monitored figures to the ledger and the filed RBC report
actions: Agree each month's opening and closing statutory surplus in the roll-forward to the general ledger statutory surplus balance for that writing company.
Agree the December TAC and ACL used in monitoring to the figures in the RBC report filed by March 1, and explain any difference by a named post-close adjustment.
Confirm every dividend and capital contribution shown in a roll-forward has a Treasury settlement record and, where applicable, a commissioner approval.
List any month where the monitored surplus differs from the ledger by more than $500K as an exception.
testing.done: monitored surplus ties to the ledger each month and the December figures tie to the filed RBC report, or the difference is written up.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of months
actions: Take 100% of months in which any trigger rung was crossed, and 100% of months containing a dividend or capital contribution.
Take 4 further months per writing company at random using a recorded seed, with a minimum of 24 company-months overall.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add every prior-test exception month as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers every trigger-crossing and capital-movement month, is reproducible from the recorded seed and includes prior-test exceptions.

testing.step: Recompute the ratio and the headroom for each sampled month
actions: Rebuild TAC for the sampled month from the ledger surplus, the AVR balance and the apportioned dividend liability without opening the production roll-forward first.
Rebuild the ACL estimate by re-applying the covariance formula to the month's components and compare to the reported estimate.
Recompute the ratio and the dollar headroom to the amber, red and Company Action Level rungs, and compare to what the dashboard published.
Any recomputation that lands on a different rung than the dashboard reported is an exception regardless of the size of the numeric difference.
testing.done: each sampled month has an independent TAC, ACL, ratio and headroom recomputation with a stated agree or disagree on the rung reported.

testing.step: Re-perform the trend test where the company sat inside the band
actions: Identify every sampled month where a life company sat between 200% and 250% of ACL or a P&C company between 200% and 300%.
Re-perform the trend test from the prior two year-end TAC figures and, for P&C, recompute the combined ratio from the annual statement Underwriting and Investment Exhibit.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded conclusion; a missed positive trend test is a reportable breach because it suppressed an RBC plan obligation.
Capture the source pages relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: every in-band month has an independently re-performed trend test with captured source pages and a stated conclusion.

testing.step: Trace each trigger crossing to a timely alert and escalation
actions: For each crossing identified by your own recomputation, find the GRC risk event and read its raised date against the month-end date.
Confirm the notification reached the recipients the appetite statement names for that rung, using the email evidence attached to the event.
Measure the elapsed business days from crossing to notification and compare to the rung's stated response time.
A crossing you found that has no event at all is the worst finding available here and is escalated immediately, not held for the report.
testing.done: every recomputed crossing traces to a risk event raised inside the rung's response time and notified to the named recipients, or is logged as a detection failure.

testing.step: Test the RBC plan obligation and its 45-day deadline maths
actions: For any Company Action Level event in the period, recompute the 45-day due date from the triggering RBC report date and compare to the actual filing date.

Read the filed plan against the Model Act's required content and confirm it carries the contributing conditions, the corrective actions, four-year projections with and without those actions, the key assumptions and the business quality discussion.
Confirm board adoption is minuted before the filing date and that the domiciliary commissioner's receipt is on file.
Confirm every state that requested a copy received one, and that the plan was handled as confidential throughout.
testing.done: each Company Action Level event has a content-complete, board-adopted plan filed within the recomputed 45-day deadline with receipt evidence.

testing.step: Test dividend and capital extraction decisions against the position
actions: For each sampled dividend, recompute the post-payment RBC ratio and confirm it was computed before the payment settled, not after.
Re-apply the domiciliary state's extraordinary dividend test to the payment amount and confirm the approval-required determination was correct.
Where approval was required, confirm the commissioner's approval or the expiry of the non-disapproval period pre-dates the settlement date.
Any extraction that took the ratio below the amber rung without a written CFO and Chief Risk Officer decision is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled extraction has a pre-settlement ratio recomputation, a correct extraordinary dividend determination and, where needed, approval pre-dating settlement.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying the writing company, month, rung involved and whether the failure was detection, escalation, filing or decision.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — late ledger close, stale ACL estimate, KRI threshold not updated after a material change, alert routed to a leaver, deadline miscomputed — and name an owner.
For any missed Company Action Level notification, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel the same week.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a failure type, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the detection rate (crossings found by recomputation versus crossings alerted) and the mean escalation lag in business days.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references and stating whether any statutory trigger went unreported.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no roll-forward under test and sits outside Finance and Capital Management, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Board Risk Committee and the Audit Committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper under Capital/Monitoring/<year>.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the detection rate, escalation lag and a conclusion exists in the repository with a committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns submission of the annual RBC report to every domiciliary and non-domiciliary state that demands it and to the NAIC by March 1; content certified by the Head of Capital Management, statement package certified by the Chief Financial Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the filing sections of Alabama's RBC for Insurers Model Act (312) adoption and the 50 parallel adoptions, requiring the RBC report to be filed with the commissioner and the NAIC on or before March 1; each state's current annual statement filing checklist is re-read every December when the NAIC publishes it

In-scope processes.value: Annual statement close → RBC report assembly → jurat and officer certification → electronic submission to the NAIC Financial Data Repository and to each state that requires a direct copy → fee payment → receipt capture → analyst inquiry response, across all 51 jurisdictions of licensure and every writing company

In-scope systems.value: The statutory reporting suite produces and validates the RBC blank; filing is made through NAIC iSite+ / the Financial Data Repository, with state fees and direct state copies routed through OPTins and the state portals the annual statement checklist names

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statutory Filing Procedure — RBC section: the per-state filing matrix (NAIC-only versus NAIC plus direct state copy, electronic versus hard copy, fee and payment channel), the cross-check clearance rule, the officer signature sequence and the receipt capture standard

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer; the per-state filing matrix is re-approved each December against the newly published NAIC annual statement filing checklists and any state bulletin changing the channel or the fee

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: RBC report and annual statement due March 1 in all 51 jurisdictions; the statutory Actuarial Opinion accompanies the March 1 statement, the audited financial statement follows by June 1, CGAD by June 1, and any amended RBC report is due immediately on determination of the error

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts at Feb 1 (draft package assembled), Feb 15 (cross-checks cleared and officers scheduled to sign), Feb 22 (submission window opens) and Feb 28 (escalate any unfiled company to the CFO), one alert per writing company per jurisdiction

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed RBC blank as submitted, the signed jurat, the NAIC Financial Data Repository confirmation, each state's receipt or acknowledgement, fee payment proof and the cross-check clearance report, retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository indexed by NAIC company code and year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any filing made after March 1, any submission rejected by the Financial Data Repository, any state receipt not captured within 5 business days, and any amended RBC report is logged with root cause, the penalty or fine assessed and the corrective date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The CFO signs off every late filing explanation, every amended RBC submission and every waiver or extension request made to a commissioner

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every writing company × jurisdiction filing obligation for the reporting year — the RBC report plus the accompanying statutory filings — as listed on the approved per-state filing matrix

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on late or missed filings — any RBC report submitted after March 1 or to the wrong channel is a fail, as is any obligation missing from the filing matrix; one fail escalates to the CFO and is reported to the Audit Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual (March 1); the test runs once a year in Q2 over the completed filing season, with a December pre-season readiness check on the per-state filing matrix against the new NAIC checklists

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Regulatory Reporting and must not have prepared or submitted any filing in the population

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual statutory filing test workpaper (obligation matrix, submission evidence, timestamp analysis, fee reconciliation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Regulatory/Filings/<reporting year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The as-filed RBC blank, signed jurat, Financial Data Repository confirmation and state acknowledgements per company per year, producible to a domiciliary examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager answers filing-mechanics questions from state financial analysts; Regulatory Counsel clears any late-filing explanation, waiver request or amended-report notification, and RBC content is transmitted only through channels that preserve its statutory confidentiality

checklist.step: Rebuild the per-state filing matrix for the season
actions: Pull the current licence list per writing company from the internal regulatory system and confirm it against the NAIC's state-of-domicile and licence records.

For each jurisdiction, open the newly published NAIC annual statement filing checklist and record what it demands for RBC: NAIC-only submission, a direct state copy, electronic or hard copy, and the fee.

Add the accompanying obligations that travel with the March 1 statement — the statutory Actuarial Opinion, the jurat, the Supplemental Compensation Exhibit and the Management Discussion and Analysis where required.
Have the Compliance Manager review the matrix for any jurisdiction added or dropped since last season and take CFO approval before the season starts.
checklist.done: an approved matrix exists showing, for every writing company and jurisdiction, the RBC channel, format, fee and accompanying filings for the current season.

checklist.step: Confirm filing credentials and entitlements before the window opens
actions: Log in to NAIC iSite+ and confirm the Financial Data Repository upload entitlement is active for every NAIC company code you must file for.
Confirm the OPTins account is funded and the bank mandate is current so state fees cannot fail on submission night.
Confirm the state portal logins named on the matrix still work and reset anything expired at least three weeks before March 1.
Record the credential check date and the entitlement list, and raise any missing entitlement to the NAIC support desk immediately rather than in the final week.
checklist.done: every NAIC company code has confirmed Financial Data Repository entitlement, a funded fee channel and working state portal access, dated at least three weeks before March 1.

checklist.step: Assemble the RBC filing package from the locked calculation
actions: Import the locked RBC calculation handed over by the Head of Capital Management into the statutory reporting suite's RBC blank for the correct formula and statement type.
Generate the full page set for the entity — Life LR pages, P&C PR pages or Health XR pages — plus the RBC summary and the Five-Year Historical RBC lines.
Confirm the version imported carries the same calculation date and factor table stamp as the locked workbook, and reject any package built from an unlocked draft.
Produce the filing PDF and the electronic submission file and store both against the company's filing record.
checklist.done: the RBC page set is generated from the locked calculation with a matching calculation date and factor stamp, and both filing formats exist on the filing record.

checklist.step: Clear every cross-check the NAIC validation raises
actions: Run the NAIC cross-check and edit validation over the combined annual statement and RBC package and export the full error and warning list.
Clear every hard error by correcting the source data, not by overriding, and re-run until the error count is zero.
Resolve every warning by either correcting it or writing an explanation into the filing note, because unexplained warnings are what draw the analyst's first question.
Hand any error rooted in the calculation back to the Capital Model Actuary for a corrected component rather than patching it in the blank.
File the final clearance report showing zero hard errors and the explanation for each remaining warning.
checklist.done: the clearance report shows zero hard errors and a written explanation against every remaining warning.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer signatures on the jurat and certification
actions: Prepare the jurat page for each writing company naming the officers the state requires — typically the president or CEO, the secretary and the treasurer or CFO.
Circulate for signature with the completed statement and RBC package attached so signatories are certifying against the actual filed content, not a summary.
Confirm the notarisation or attestation wording each domiciliary state demands and apply it exactly.
Track signature status daily from Feb 15 and escalate any officer not signed by Feb 22 to the CFO.
checklist.done: every writing company has a fully executed jurat, in the domiciliary state's required form, dated before submission.

checklist.step: Submit the RBC report to the NAIC Financial Data Repository
actions: In NAIC iSite+ open the Financial Data Repository upload for the reporting year and select the annual RBC filing type for the company's formula.
Upload the submission file, confirm the NAIC company code, statement type and reporting period shown on the confirmation screen match the entity, and submit.
Save the submission confirmation with its timestamp and confirmation number to the filing record immediately — this is the primary evidence of the March 1 deadline being met.
Re-run the upload the same day if the repository returns a rejection, and log the rejection as an exception even where the re-file lands before March 1.
checklist.done: every writing company has a Financial Data Repository confirmation number and timestamp on or before March 1 saved to its filing record.

checklist.step: File the direct state copies the matrix requires
actions: Work the matrix jurisdiction by jurisdiction, filing the RBC report directly wherever the state's checklist demands a copy in addition to the NAIC submission.
Use the exact channel the checklist names — the state's own portal, a secure email address, or paper to the department's financial analysis unit — and never substitute a channel because it is easier.
Mark every transmission confidential in line with the Model Act's confidentiality section so the copy is not treated as a public record.
Capture the acknowledgement, portal receipt or delivery confirmation against the jurisdiction row within 5 business days.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction requiring a direct copy shows a dated transmission through the named channel with a captured receipt.

checklist.step: Pay the filing fees and reconcile them
actions: Pay each jurisdiction's annual statement and RBC-related fee through OPTins or the channel the state's checklist names, using the fee amount published for the current season.
Reconcile the total paid to the matrix's expected fee schedule and investigate any difference over $100 before the season closes.
Attach the payment confirmation to the jurisdiction row, since several states treat the filing as incomplete until the fee clears.
Ask the Controller to book the fees to the regulatory fees account so the year's cost reconciles to the matrix.
checklist.done: every fee-bearing jurisdiction shows a cleared payment confirmation reconciled to the expected fee schedule.

checklist.step: Confirm the accompanying statutory filings landed with the statement
actions: Confirm the Appointed Actuary's statutory Actuarial Opinion was filed with the March 1 statement in every state that requires it, and record where the supporting Actuarial Opinion Memorandum will be available on request.
Confirm the annual statement itself, the jurat and any state-specific supplements on the matrix were filed to the same deadline.

Diary the follow-on solvency filings so they are not lost after the March 1 rush: the audited financial statement and the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure by June 1, and the ORSA Summary Report on the lead state's agreed date.
Report the completed March 1 position — filed, receipted and paid — to the CFO within 5 business days of the deadline.
checklist.done: the March 1 package is confirmed complete per company per state and the follow-on solvency filings are diarised with owners.

checklist.step: Chase and capture every outstanding receipt
actions: Run the matrix on 5 March and list every jurisdiction row without a captured receipt or acknowledgement.
Chase the department's financial analysis contact by the channel used for the filing and record the date and person contacted.
Raise a tracker issue for any receipt still missing 10 business days after filing, since an unproven filing is treated as an unmade filing at examination.
Close each row only when the receipt is attached, not when the chase email is sent.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction row carries a captured receipt, or an open tracker issue with a named contact and chase history.

checklist.step: File an amended RBC report the moment an error is found
actions: On notification from Capital Management or a state analyst that a filed figure is wrong, quantify the effect on ACL, TAC and the RBC ratio and whether it changes an action level conclusion.
Have the Chief Actuary sign the corrected calculation and Regulatory Counsel clear the notification wording before anything is transmitted.
Re-file the amended RBC report through the Financial Data Repository marked as an amendment and notify the domiciliary analyst in writing the same day.
Log the amendment as an exception with root cause and confirm every state that received a direct copy receives the amendment too.
checklist.done: each amendment is signed, counsel-cleared, re-filed through the repository and notified to the domiciliary analyst and every direct-copy state on the same day.

checklist.step: Handle state analyst inquiries arising from the filing
actions: Log every inquiry from a financial analysis unit with the state, the date received, the question and the department's stated due date.
Draft the answer with the component owner named on the RBC control sheet and verify every figure against the as-filed blank before responding.
Respond inside the department's due date and, where more time is needed, request an extension in writing before the date passes rather than after.
File the inquiry, the response and its supporting schedules under the company's filing record.
checklist.done: every analyst inquiry has a logged, figure-verified response sent inside the department's due date or a pre-expiry written extension.

checklist.step: Preserve the confidentiality the Model Act attaches to RBC information
actions: Confirm every transmission of the RBC report carried the confidentiality marking and travelled through a channel the department accepts for confidential material.
Confirm no RBC level, ratio or comparison appears in advertising, sales literature, rating agency presentations or investor material, which the Model Act's prohibition section forbids.
Review any third-party request for the RBC report and refuse or route it to the department rather than releasing it.
Record the confidentiality review with the date and reviewer on the season's filing record.
checklist.done: a dated confidentiality review confirms every transmission was marked and routed correctly and no RBC level appears in any public or promotional material.

checklist.step: Run the post-season debrief and update the matrix
actions: Within 20 business days of March 1 review every rejection, late receipt, fee difference and analyst inquiry from the season.
Update the per-state filing matrix for any channel, format or fee change the season revealed, and note the source bulletin or checklist page.
Agree owners and dates for process fixes — credential expiry, cross-check clearance timing, signature scheduling — and load them into the tracker.
Present the debrief to the CFO before the next season's matrix approval.
checklist.done: the debrief is complete, the matrix is updated with sourced changes, and every process fix has an owner and a date in the tracker.

checklist.step: Archive the season's filing evidence
actions: File the as-filed RBC blank, signed jurat, cross-check clearance report, Financial Data Repository confirmation, every state receipt and every fee proof under Regulatory/Filings/<reporting year>/<NAIC company code>.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm the index makes records retrievable by NAIC company code, jurisdiction and reporting year.
Reconcile the archived record count to the matrix row count and close the season only when they agree.
Notify the Chief Audit Executive that the season's evidence is complete and available for test.
checklist.done: archived evidence matches the matrix row count exactly, is labelled for 7-year retention and is retrievable by company code and jurisdiction.

testing.step: Build the population of filing obligations independently of the matrix
actions: Derive the obligation population from the licence records — every writing company × every jurisdiction where it held a licence during the reporting year — rather than from the filing matrix, so a missing matrix row is detectable.
Overlay the NAIC annual statement filing checklists for the season to determine what each jurisdiction demanded for RBC.
Compare your derived population to the approved matrix and list every row present in one and absent from the other as an exception before sampling.
testing.done: an independently derived obligation population exists and every difference against the approved matrix is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the source of record for filings made
actions: Extract the Financial Data Repository submission history for every NAIC company code for the reporting year and reconcile it to the population's NAIC-submission rows.
Reconcile the direct-copy rows to the archived state receipts under Regulatory/Filings/<reporting year>.
Reconcile the fee payments to the OPTins transaction history and to the regulatory fees account in the general ledger.
Any obligation with no submission evidence is an automatic exception, and any submission with no obligation row is investigated as a scope error.
testing.done: every obligation reconciles to a repository submission, a state receipt and a fee payment, or is written up.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of filings
actions: Take 100% of domiciliary state filings, 100% of rows that were rejected or re-filed, and 100% of amended RBC reports.
Take 20 further jurisdiction rows at random using a recorded seed, stratified across writing companies, for a minimum sample of 35 rows.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date so the sample is reproducible.
Add every prior-year exception row as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: the sample covers all domiciliary, rejected and amended rows, is reproducible from the seed and carries forward prior-year exceptions.

testing.step: Re-perform the deadline test on every sampled submission
actions: Read the confirmation timestamp on the Financial Data Repository submission or the state receipt for each sampled row.
Compare it to March 1 of the filing year in the department's own time zone, since a submission after midnight local time is late even if the system accepted it.
Where an extension was granted, confirm a written grant from the department pre-dates March 1; a verbal assurance is not evidence.
Record days early or late for each row so the season's timing profile is visible, not just the pass or fail.
testing.done: each sampled row has a timestamp-to-deadline comparison in the department's time zone with days early or late recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the content check against the as-filed blank
actions: Open the as-filed RBC blank for each sampled row and confirm the page set matches the entity's formula and statement type.
Agree the filed ACL and TAC to the locked calculation workbook archived by Capital Management, and to the Five-Year Historical page in the filed annual statement.
Confirm the cross-check clearance report attached to the row shows zero hard errors at the time of filing.
Confirm the jurat is fully executed by the officers the domiciliary state names and dated before the submission timestamp.
testing.done: each sampled filing's page set, ACL, TAC, clearance report and executed jurat agree with the locked calculation and pre-date submission.

testing.step: Trace each sampled row to a receipt and an identifier
actions: For each sampled row, locate the confirmation number, portal receipt or department acknowledgement in the archive.
Confirm the identifier on the receipt matches the NAIC company code and reporting year of the row, since misdirected filings usually surface here.
Measure the elapsed days from filing to receipt capture and flag anything beyond the 5-business-day standard.
Treat a row whose only evidence is an internal note that the filing was made as an unproven filing and an exception.
testing.done: every sampled row has a receipt bearing the matching company code and year, captured within the 5-business-day standard or logged.

testing.step: Recompute the fee amounts and the follow-on filing deadlines
actions: Recompute each sampled jurisdiction's fee from the state's published fee schedule for the season and compare to the amount paid.

Recompute the follow-on solvency deadlines the March 1 filing sets up — audited financial statement and CGAD by June 1, the ORSA Summary Report on the lead state's agreed date — and confirm each was met.
Where an amended RBC report was filed, confirm it went out on the day the error was determined and reached every direct-copy state.
List any over- or under-payment above $100 and any missed follow-on deadline as exceptions.
testing.done: fees reconcile to the published schedules and every follow-on solvency deadline is recomputed and confirmed met or logged.

testing.step: Test the confidentiality handling of the filed information
actions: Sample the transmissions for the direct-copy states and confirm each carried the confidentiality marking and used an accepted secure channel.
Search the year's advertising, sales literature, rating agency decks and investor material for any RBC level, ratio or comparison and confirm none appears.
Review any third-party request for the RBC report received in the year and confirm it was refused or routed to the department.
Treat any appearance of an RBC level in promotional material as a Model Act breach, not a marketing review point.
testing.done: sampled transmissions were marked and securely routed, and no RBC level appears in any promotional, rating or investor material.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying the writing company, jurisdiction, obligation type and whether the failure was timeliness, channel, content, fee or evidence.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — matrix row missing, credential expired, cross-check cleared late, officer signature late, receipt never chased — and name an owner.
Record any penalty, fine or department comment received, and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any missed statutory deadline.
Carry every open exception into next season's pre-filing readiness check as a mandatory verification.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a failure type, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a pre-season retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and the receipt capture rate against the zero-tolerance timeliness threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references and naming any jurisdiction filed late or through the wrong channel.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and submitted none of the sampled filings and sits outside Regulatory Reporting, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under Regulatory/Filings/<reporting year>.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the on-time rate, receipt capture rate and a conclusion exists in the repository with an Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns and signs the ORSA Summary Report; Section 3 group capital modelling delegated to the Capital Model Actuary, board adoption stewarded by the Corporate Secretary
