Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the NAIC Risk Management and Own Risk and Solvency Assessment Model Act (#505) as adopted in the domiciliary state, read with the current NAIC ORSA Guidance Manual, alongside the RBC Model Act (312) adoptions that the capital adequacy sections feed; the premium exemption thresholds ($500M individual, $1B group) are retested every year

In-scope processes.value: Annual risk identification and appetite refresh → Section 1 risk management framework description → Section 2 quantitative assessment of each material risk under normal and stressed conditions → Section 3 group risk capital and three-to-five-year prospective solvency assessment → board challenge and adoption → lead state filing, covering every insurer in the group across the 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Risk register, appetite thresholds, control assessments and risk events feed Sections 1 and 2; the economic and RBC capital projections come from the capital model, and the report is issued to directors through the board portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: ORSA Procedure — the exemption test, the three-section content map to the ORSA Guidance Manual, the risk materiality threshold, the group capital aggregation method, the prospective solvency projection horizon and assumptions, the board challenge protocol and the lead state filing route

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board Risk Committee; re-approved annually before the assessment cycle opens and whenever the NAIC updates the ORSA Guidance Manual or the group acquires, disposes of or re-domesticates an insurer

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: One ORSA Summary Report per year filed with the lead state on the date agreed with it, with the internal timetable backed off that date: risk refresh complete 20 weeks prior, Section 2 modelling 12 weeks prior, draft to the Board Risk Committee 8 weeks prior, board adoption 4 weeks prior; a copy goes to any non-lead domiciliary commissioner on request

Deadline reminders configured.value: ORSA cycle milestones loaded into the GRC platform with owner alerts at each of the 20-, 12-, 8- and 4-week gates, plus a hard alert to the Chief Risk Officer if board adoption has not been minuted 10 business days before the agreed filing date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The filed ORSA Summary Report, the risk register extract and appetite statement it was built from, the model runs and assumption sets behind Sections 2 and 3, the board pack, the minuted adoption resolution and the lead state receipt, retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any material risk omitted from Section 2, any Section 3 projection built on an unvalidated model, any filing made without a minuted board resolution and any late filing against the lead state's agreed date is logged with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Board Governance Lead confirms that every board challenge point raised at adoption is answered and evidenced before the report is filed, and signs off any post-filing correction

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The ORSA Summary Report filed in the year, decomposed into every material risk in the register, every Section 2 quantification and every Section 3 projection scenario, plus the exemption test performed for each insurer in the group

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on completeness — any risk above the materiality threshold absent from Section 2, any projection whose model has no current validation, or any filing without a minuted board adoption is a fail; one fail escalates to the Board Risk Committee chair

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual; the test runs once per cycle after filing, with a mid-cycle readiness review of the risk register and model validation status so gaps surface before the report is written

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Risk Management and Capital Management and must not have authored any section of the report under test

Evidence location for test results.value: ORSA verification workpaper (risk completeness matrix, Section 2 re-performance, Section 3 projection recomputation, board minute trace, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Risk/ORSA/<cycle year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The filed ORSA Summary Report with its supporting model documentation, assumption register and board minutes, producible to the lead state's ORSA reviewer within 10 business days and structured to the ORSA Guidance Manual's three sections

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer leads the lead state's ORSA review meeting; Regulatory Counsel confirms the report is handled under the Model Act's confidentiality section, and no ORSA content is shared with rating agencies or investors without counsel clearance

checklist.step: Retest the ORSA filing exemption for every insurer in the group
actions: Pull each insurer's annual direct plus assumed written premium from the filed annual statement, excluding premiums ceded to affiliates as the Model Act directs.
Test each insurer against the $500M individual threshold and the group against the $1B threshold, and record the tested figures and the conclusion.
Where an insurer is exempt but the group is not, confirm it is still covered inside the group ORSA rather than dropped entirely.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the domiciliary state has not adopted a lower threshold or a waiver condition, and file the exemption memo with the cycle.
checklist.done: a dated exemption memo shows the tested premium figures, the threshold applied per entity and the group, and counsel confirmation of the state's adopted thresholds.

checklist.step: Agree the filing date and scope with the lead state
actions: Confirm which state is lead state for the group under the NAIC lead state framework and identify the department's ORSA contact.
Confirm in writing the agreed annual filing date and whether the department wants the report by secure portal or encrypted transmission.
Ask which non-lead domiciliary states, if any, have requested a copy this cycle and record them on the distribution list.
Load the agreed date into the GRC cycle plan and back off the 20-, 12-, 8- and 4-week internal gates from it.
checklist.done: the lead state, its ORSA contact, the agreed filing date, the transmission channel and the distribution list are confirmed in writing and loaded into the cycle plan.

checklist.step: Refresh the risk register and the materiality threshold
actions: Run risk identification workshops with Underwriting, Claims, Investments, Actuarial, Operations and Technology and update the register's inherent and residual scores.
Set the materiality threshold in dollar terms for the cycle — commonly a percentage of statutory surplus agreed with the Board Risk Committee — and mark every risk above it as ORSA-material.
Confirm every ORSA-material risk has a named owner, a stated appetite limit and a current control assessment; anything without them goes back to the owner before modelling starts.
Extract the ORSA-material risk list as a dated snapshot so the report and the test both point at the same list.
checklist.done: a dated snapshot lists every ORSA-material risk with an owner, an appetite limit and a current control assessment, against an agreed dollar materiality threshold.

checklist.step: Write Section 1 — the risk management framework description
actions: Describe the framework against the ORSA Guidance Manual's five elements: risk culture and governance, risk identification and prioritisation, risk appetite and tolerances with limits, risk management and controls, and risk reporting and communication.
Name the committees, their charters, their meeting frequency and the reporting lines from the first line to the board, rather than describing an ideal structure.
State the appetite and tolerance figures actually in force, including the RBC ratio triggers, and cross-reference the appetite statement approved by the Board Risk Committee.
Describe how the framework changed since the prior cycle and why, since the lead state reads year-on-year change closely.
checklist.done: Section 1 covers all five Guidance Manual elements with named committees, in-force appetite figures and a stated year-on-year change narrative.

checklist.step: Quantify each material risk under normal conditions for Section 2
actions: Take the ORSA-material risk snapshot and assign each risk to a quantification method: modelled distribution, deterministic scenario or documented qualitative assessment where no defensible model exists.
Run the base case on the current in-force and the approved business plan, producing the exposure measure and the capital held against each risk.
State the metric and the confidence level used for each risk — for example value at risk at 99.5% over one year, or tail value at risk — and keep it consistent across the report.
Document the assumption set, the data as-of date and the model version for every quantification into the model governance repository.
checklist.done: every ORSA-material risk has a base-case quantification with a stated metric, confidence level, assumption set and archived model version.

checklist.step: Quantify the same risks under stressed conditions
actions: Apply the approved stress and scenario set to each material risk and record the post-stress capital requirement and available capital.
Show the combined effect where risks correlate — an equity fall arriving with a credit spread widening and a reserve strengthening is the case the reviewer will look for.
Compare the post-stress position to the appetite limits and to the RBC action levels, stating the ratio and the dollar headroom in each scenario.
Have the Chief Risk Officer confirm the stress severities are consistent with the risk appetite statement before the results are drafted into the report.
checklist.done: each material risk shows a post-stress requirement, a post-stress RBC ratio and a comparison to appetite limits, with correlated scenarios included.

checklist.step: Build the Section 3 group risk capital assessment
actions: Aggregate the risk quantifications to a group risk capital figure using the approved aggregation method, and disclose the method, the correlation assumptions and the diversification benefit claimed.
Reconcile group risk capital to the sum of the entities' RBC requirements and explain the difference, since the lead state will compare the two.
Compare available capital to required capital at group and at each material entity, and state the surplus or shortfall in dollars.

Disclose any capital that is not fungible across the group — trapped in a subsidiary, restricted by a state dividend rule or committed as reinsurance collateral — because ignoring fungibility overstates group capital.
checklist.done: Section 3 states group risk capital, the aggregation method and diversification benefit, a reconciliation to entity RBC, and the non-fungible capital excluded.

checklist.step: Run the prospective solvency assessment over the planning horizon
actions: Project available and required capital over the three-to-five-year business plan horizon on the plan case, using the volumes, pricing and investment assumptions the board approved.
Repeat the projection on the stress cases and identify the first year in which any entity's projected RBC ratio would fall below the internal amber trigger or the Company Action Level.
State the management actions assumed in the projection — reinsurance purchase, dividend suspension, capital injection — and confirm each is genuinely available rather than aspirational.
Have the Chief Financial Officer confirm the plan assumptions used match the board-approved business plan, and archive the projection run id.
checklist.done: the projection covers the plan horizon on plan and stress cases, names the first breach year in each, lists only genuinely available management actions and is CFO-confirmed against the approved plan.

checklist.step: Validate the models behind Sections 2 and 3 before they enter the report
actions: List every model feeding the report and confirm each carries a validation dated inside the governance cycle with no open high-severity finding.
Test the material assumptions for support: check the calibration data, the expert judgements and their sign-off, and the back-test results where the model has history.
Confirm the data feeding each model reconciles to the statutory or ledger source it claims, and quantify any unreconciled amount.
Issue a validation opinion naming any quantification the report should present with a caveat, and give it to the Chief Risk Officer before drafting closes.
checklist.done: every model behind Sections 2 and 3 has a current validation, supported assumptions, reconciled data and a written opinion with any required caveats.

checklist.step: Draft the ORSA Summary Report against the Guidance Manual structure
actions: Assemble the three sections in the Guidance Manual's order with a content map showing which paragraph answers which Manual requirement.
State plainly the group's own conclusion on capital adequacy over the planning horizon — the Manual expects a conclusion, not a data dump.
Include the methodology, assumptions and data quality commentary that lets a reviewer reproduce the numbers, and mark every figure's as-of date.
Circulate the draft to the CFO, Chief Actuary, Chief Investment Officer and General Counsel for review and log each comment with its disposition.
checklist.done: a complete draft exists with a Manual content map, a stated capital adequacy conclusion, reproducible methodology and a logged disposition for every reviewer comment.

checklist.step: Take the report through Board Risk Committee challenge
actions: Publish the draft, the risk snapshot and the projection outputs to the board portal at least 8 weeks before the agreed filing date and 5 business days before the meeting.
Present the material risks, the stressed positions, the first projected breach year and the management actions assumed, and invite the committee to challenge severities and assumptions.
Minute every challenge point with an owner and a response date, and re-run any quantification the committee asks to see differently.
Return the revised report to the committee for confirmation that its points have been answered before it goes to the board.
checklist.done: committee challenge is minuted point by point, each point has an evidenced response and the committee has confirmed its points are answered.

checklist.step: Obtain board adoption and the officer attestation
actions: Table the final report for board adoption at least 4 weeks before the agreed filing date, with the committee's confirmation attached.
Minute a resolution that names the report, its cycle year and the board's adoption of the risk management framework and the capital adequacy conclusion it states.
Obtain the Chief Risk Officer's signed attestation page as the Guidance Manual expects, dated on or after the adoption date.
File the minute extract and the signed attestation with the report package before any transmission is made.
checklist.done: a minuted adoption resolution naming the report and a signed CRO attestation dated on or after adoption sit in the report package.

checklist.step: File the report with the lead state and any requesting commissioner
actions: Transmit the adopted report to the lead state's ORSA contact through the agreed secure channel on or before the agreed date, marked confidential under the Model Act.
Send copies to each non-lead domiciliary commissioner on the distribution list and record the date and channel for each.
Capture the receipt or acknowledgement from every recipient within 5 business days and attach it to the cycle record.
Notify the Chief Risk Officer and the Board Governance Lead once every recipient has acknowledged.
checklist.done: the lead state and every listed commissioner have received the report on or before the agreed date with acknowledgements captured.

checklist.step: Work the lead state's review feedback back into the framework
actions: Log every question and observation from the lead state's ORSA review meeting with the date, the reviewer and the requested response date.
Answer each with the supporting model run, assumption or minute, and never with a narrative that the report already contained.
Convert observations about framework weakness into dated remediation actions in the GRC platform with named owners, and report progress to the Board Risk Committee.
Carry the open observations into the next cycle's plan so the following report can show what changed.
checklist.done: every lead state question has an evidenced answer and every framework observation has a dated GRC action with an owner and committee reporting.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle evidence for the retention period
actions: File the filed report, the exemption memo, the dated risk snapshot, the model runs and assumption sets, the validation opinion, the board pack, the adoption minute, the attestation and every receipt under Risk/ORSA/<cycle year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm the record is retrievable by cycle year, legal entity and material risk.
Confirm the model governance repository holds the archived run ids referenced in the report so a reviewer can be pointed straight at them.
Notify the Chief Audit Executive that the cycle evidence is complete and available for test.
checklist.done: the full cycle package is archived under a 7-year label, retrievable by year and entity, with report references resolving to archived model run ids.

testing.step: Build the population of material risks and report assertions
actions: Extract the risk register as at the cycle's materiality snapshot date and list every risk scoring above the agreed dollar threshold, independently of the list the report used.
Add every Section 2 quantification, every Section 3 aggregation component and every projection scenario in the filed report as separate population rows.
Add the exemption test performed for each insurer in the group so scope decisions are testable too.
testing.done: the population holds every above-threshold register risk, every report quantification and projection, and every entity exemption test.

testing.step: Reconcile the report's risk coverage to the register and the financials
actions: Match each above-threshold register risk to a Section 2 quantification; any unmatched risk is an automatic completeness exception.
Reconcile the available capital figures in Section 3 to the filed statutory surplus and Total Adjusted Capital for each entity, and explain any difference by a named adjustment.
Reconcile the premium figures used in the exemption test to the filed annual statements.
List any risk quantified in the report that has no register entry, since that signals the register is not the source of record it claims to be.
testing.done: every above-threshold risk is matched to a quantification and Section 3 capital ties to filed surplus and TAC, or the difference is written up.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of quantifications
actions: Take 100% of the five largest risks by capital held and 100% of risks whose quantification method changed since the prior cycle.
Take 8 further quantifications at random using a recorded seed, spread across modelled, deterministic and qualitative methods, for a minimum of 15 rows.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add every prior-cycle exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers the five largest risks and all method changes, is reproducible from the seed and carries forward prior-cycle exceptions.

testing.step: Re-perform the sampled quantifications from the archived model runs
actions: Open the archived run id the report cites for each sampled quantification and confirm the run exists, is the version cited, and has not been re-run since the report date.
Re-execute the run on the archived assumption set and compare the output to the figure printed in the report.
Confirm the stated metric and confidence level match what the model actually produced, since a value at risk figure labelled as a tail value at risk misstates the tail.
Any figure in the report that cannot be reproduced from an archived run is an exception regardless of whether it looks reasonable.
testing.done: each sampled figure is reproduced from its cited archived run at the stated metric and confidence level, or logged as unreproducible.

testing.step: Re-perform the group aggregation and the diversification benefit
actions: Rebuild the group risk capital figure from the sampled component quantifications using the aggregation method the report discloses.
Recompute the diversification benefit as the difference between the simple sum of components and the aggregated figure, and compare to the benefit disclosed.
Test the correlation assumptions for support — an assumed correlation with no calibration evidence behind it is an exception, because it directly reduces stated required capital.
Confirm the non-fungible capital disclosed was actually excluded from group available capital rather than merely mentioned.
testing.done: group risk capital and the diversification benefit are independently reproduced, correlation assumptions are evidenced and non-fungible capital is confirmed excluded.

testing.step: Recompute the prospective solvency projection and its breach years
actions: Agree the projection's opening capital, premium volumes and investment return assumptions to the board-approved business plan.
Recompute the projected RBC ratio for each year of the horizon on the plan case and at least two stress cases from the projected TAC and ACL.
Identify the first year any entity's projected ratio falls below the internal amber trigger or 200% of ACL and compare to the breach year the report states.

Test whether each assumed management action is genuinely available — confirm a reinsurance placement is quoted, a capital injection is committed by the parent, a dividend suspension is within the board's power — and treat unsupported actions as an overstatement of resilience.
testing.done: projection assumptions tie to the approved plan, ratios and first breach years are independently recomputed, and every assumed management action is evidenced as available.

testing.step: Trace the report to board adoption and the filing evidence
actions: Read the board minute and confirm it names the report and cycle year and records adoption, not merely receipt of a presentation.
Confirm the Chief Risk Officer's signed attestation is dated on or after the adoption date and refers to the version actually filed.
Compare the document hash or version identifier of the filed report to the version tabled at the board; a later edit after adoption is an exception.
Confirm the lead state receipt and every distribution-list acknowledgement are on file with dates on or before the agreed filing date.
testing.done: the filed version matches the adopted version, adoption is minuted, the attestation post-dates adoption and every recipient acknowledgement is on file.

testing.step: Recompute the exemption test and the cycle deadline maths
actions: Recompute each insurer's direct plus assumed written premium from the filed annual statement, excluding affiliate cessions, and re-apply the $500M and $1B thresholds.
Confirm any insurer treated as exempt is nonetheless covered within the group report, and that no non-exempt insurer was omitted.
Recompute the internal gate dates from the lead state's agreed filing date and compare each to the actual date the gate closed.
List any gate missed by more than 5 business days, since a compressed cycle is what produces an unchallenged report.
testing.done: the exemption conclusion is independently reproduced for every insurer and every cycle gate is recomputed against the agreed filing date.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a risk event per exception carrying the cycle year, the section affected, the risk or entity involved and whether the failure was completeness, reproducibility, governance or timeliness.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — risk omitted from the snapshot, model validation lapsed, assumption unsupported, report edited after adoption, gate compressed — and name an owner.
Where a material risk was omitted or a figure is unreproducible, notify the Board Risk Committee chair the same week and assess whether the lead state must be told.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's readiness review as a mandatory verification.
testing.done: every exception has an event, a failure type, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a next-cycle retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the risk coverage rate and the figure reproducibility rate against the zero-tolerance completeness threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references and stating whether the filed report fairly represents the group's capital position.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no section and sits outside Risk and Capital Management, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Board Risk Committee and the Audit Committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper under Risk/ORSA/<cycle year>.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the coverage rate, reproducibility rate and a conclusion exists in the repository with a committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the stress and scenario testing programme feeding RBC forecasting and the ORSA; scenario design shared with the Chief Risk Officer, cat scenarios run by the CAT Modeler, asset adequacy scenarios owned by the Appointed Actuary

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the RBC Model Act (312) adoptions that make the C-3 Phase I and Phase II scenario testing and the P&C Rcat modelled-loss charge part of the calculation, read with the current-year NAIC RBC instructions, the Valuation Manual asset adequacy requirements (VM-30) and Actuarial Guideline 53 for the asset adequacy testing filing

In-scope processes.value: Annual scenario design and calibration → interest rate, equity, credit spread, catastrophe, pandemic, reserve deterioration, reinsurer default and liquidity runs → reverse stress test to the point of capital failure → translation into post-stress ACL, TAC and RBC ratio → management action selection, feeding the Section 2 stressed quantifications in the ORSA and the year-end RBC C-3 and Rcat components across all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Liability and cash flow projection runs for C-3 Phase I/II and asset adequacy; catastrophe runs in the licensed cat model; asset shocks sourced from the investment book of record; results archived against run ids in the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Stress and Scenario Testing Procedure — the scenario library and its severity calibration basis, the prescribed NAIC scenario sets that must be run unchanged, the in-house scenario approval route, the correlation rules for combined scenarios, the reverse stress test method and the reporting pack contents

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board Risk Committee on the Chief Actuary's and Chief Risk Officer's recommendation; severities are re-calibrated and re-approved every year before the cycle opens and after any event that exceeded a modelled severity

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Scenario results must be complete in time to feed the year-end RBC C-3 and Rcat components for the March 1 filing, the Appointed Actuary's opinion filed with the March 1 statement, the AG 53 asset adequacy testing supporting documentation due April 1 where applicable, and the Section 2 stressed quantifications on the ORSA cycle timetable

Deadline reminders configured.value: Model calendar alerts at Oct 1 (scenario set approved), Nov 15 (exposure and in-force data cut), Jan 15 (all runs complete), Feb 1 (results into the RBC components) and Mar 20 (AG 53 documentation drafted for the April 1 date)

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Scenario definitions with their calibration basis, model version and run id per scenario, input data extracts, result sets, the reverse stress test point, the management action assessment and the board reporting pack, retained 7 years in the model governance repository and the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any prescribed NAIC scenario altered or omitted, any run whose input data does not reconcile to the statutory source, any result used in RBC or the ORSA without an archived run id, and any scenario whose severity was not re-calibrated after being exceeded by a real event

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Model Risk Manager signs off every re-run, re-calibration and correction, and confirms the corrected result was carried through to the RBC components and the ORSA before the finding is closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every scenario in the approved library run for the cycle — prescribed NAIC scenario sets, in-house deterministic scenarios, stochastic runs and the reverse stress test — across every legal entity and every risk they cover

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on prescribed scenarios — any NAIC-prescribed scenario altered, omitted or run on a superseded model is a fail; any input extract failing to reconcile to the statutory source by more than 1% of the exposure base is a fail; any result used downstream without an archived run id is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual, tied to the March 1 RBC filing and the ORSA cycle; the test runs annually over the completed scenario set, with an interim check on the Q3 forecast runs to confirm the same scenario library and severities are in use

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit in second-line model risk, outside Actuarial and Capital Management, and must not have built, calibrated or executed any scenario under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Stress testing verification workpaper (scenario population, prescribed-scenario integrity check, input reconciliation, re-executed runs, downstream trace, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Risk/StressTesting/<cycle year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Scenario definitions, calibration basis, model documentation, run ids and result sets supporting the C-3 and Rcat components and the ORSA Section 2 stresses, producible to a financial examiner or the lead state's ORSA reviewer within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Actuary answers questions on scenario design and results, with the Appointed Actuary answering on asset adequacy and AG 53; Regulatory Counsel clears any disclosure of scenario results outside the regulator, which stay confidential under the Model Act

checklist.step: Approve the scenario library and its severity calibration for the cycle
actions: List the scenarios that must be run unchanged because a regulator prescribes them — the C-3 Phase I interest rate scenarios, the C-3 Phase II stochastic scenario set, and the return periods the RBC instructions require for the Rcat charge.

List the in-house scenarios that cover the group's material risks and state each one's severity and the calibration basis behind it — a historical event, a return period, or an expert judgement with its sign-off.
Map every ORSA-material risk to at least one scenario so no material risk goes unstressed, and record the gaps you are consciously accepting.
Take the library to the Board Risk Committee by 1 October for approval and load the approved list into the GRC platform as the cycle's scope.
checklist.done: an approved library exists by 1 October separating prescribed from in-house scenarios, with a calibration basis per scenario and every material risk mapped.

checklist.step: Cut and reconcile the data the scenarios will run on
actions: Extract the in-force liability data as at the agreed data cut date by product, guarantee type, surrender charge status and reserve basis.
Extract the year-to-date asset holdings file by CUSIP, NAIC designation, book and market value from the investment book of record.
Reconcile the liability extract to Exhibit 5 or Schedule P and the asset extract to Schedule D and Schedule BA; anything off by more than 1% of the exposure base goes back before a run starts.
Publish the reconciled extracts with a data-cut timestamp so every scenario in the cycle runs on the same base.
checklist.done: one timestamped, reconciled liability and asset base exists for the cycle, tying to the statutory schedules within 1% of the exposure base.

checklist.step: Run the prescribed interest rate scenarios without modification
actions: Load the current-year prescribed scenario file for C-3 Phase I and run the deterministic rising, falling and pop-up/pop-down paths on the reconciled model points.
Run the C-3 Phase II stochastic scenario set for variable annuity and guaranteed living benefit business at the prescribed scenario count and confidence level.
Record the resulting C-3 charge, the worst scenario, and the surplus at the tail measure the instructions specify.
Do not adjust a prescribed path or scenario weight; where a model limitation prevents a faithful run, record it as a limitation and tell the Model Risk Manager rather than substituting your own path.
checklist.done: the prescribed interest rate and stochastic sets are run unmodified on the reconciled base, with the resulting charge, worst scenario and any model limitation recorded.

checklist.step: Run the equity and market shock scenarios
actions: Apply the approved equity shocks to the holdings file at the severities the library sets — for example an immediate 30% and 40% fall in public equity with the corresponding move in alternatives and private equity marks.
Apply the approved real estate and Schedule BA marks and revalue the portfolio, holding the liability side constant so the pure asset effect is visible.
Compute the effect on statutory surplus, on the AVR balance, and on the C-1cs / R2 charge as designations and values move.
Hand the shocked holdings file to the Capital Model Actuary with the shock definition attached so the charge can be rebuilt, not just the surplus.
checklist.done: each equity and market shock produces a revalued holdings file, a surplus effect and a recomputed asset risk charge, with the shock definition attached.

checklist.step: Run the credit spread widening and default scenario
actions: Apply the approved spread widening by rating band to the fixed income portfolio and revalue, recording the market value effect separately from the statutory carrying effect.
Apply the approved downgrade migration matrix, move holdings between NAIC designation categories, and recompute the C-1o / R1 charge on the migrated designations.
Apply the assumed default and recovery rates to the lowest-quality tranche and compute the impairment that would flow through statutory surplus.
Reconcile the shocked portfolio back to the base holdings file so no bond appears or disappears in the scenario.
checklist.done: the credit scenario produces a spread revaluation, a designation-migration recomputation of the asset charge and an impairment effect on surplus, reconciled to the base holdings.

checklist.step: Run the catastrophe scenarios at the required return periods
actions: Run the reconciled exposure through the hurricane, earthquake and severe convective storm models and pull the occurrence and aggregate exceedance probability curves.

Apply the in-force reinsurance structure supplied by the Reinsurance Manager to produce net losses at the 1-in-100 and 1-in-250 return periods, including reinstatement premium and any exhausted-layer effect.
Run the multi-event year scenario the library defines, since a single 1-in-100 rarely exhausts a programme but two mid-sized events often do.
Hand the net loss table to the Capital Model Actuary for the Rcat pages and record the model version, event set and run id.
checklist.done: net catastrophe losses at the required return periods and the multi-event year are produced from a named model run reflecting the in-force reinsurance structure.

checklist.step: Run the insurance risk scenarios on mortality, morbidity and lapse
actions: Apply the approved pandemic mortality shock to the life in-force and compute the claims cost, the reserve movement and the reinsurance recovery.
Apply the approved morbidity deterioration to disability and long-term care blocks, and the approved longevity improvement to annuity blocks, since those move surplus in opposite directions.
Apply the dynamic lapse scenario in combination with the interest rate paths, because lapse behaviour and rates cannot sensibly be stressed independently for products with surrender options.
Record the reserve effect, the C-2 charge effect and the net-of-reinsurance surplus effect for each scenario.
checklist.done: each insurance risk scenario shows a reserve effect, a C-2 charge effect and a net-of-reinsurance surplus effect on the reconciled in-force.

checklist.step: Run the reserve deterioration and reinsurer default scenarios
actions: Apply the approved adverse development percentage by line of business to net carried reserves and recompute the R4 reserve risk charge on the strengthened reserves.
Model the failure of the single largest reinsurer: write off the uncollateralised recoverable, recompute the credit risk charge and recompute the net position on the treaties it supported.
Model the failure of the largest two reinsurers together where the programme concentrates, since concentration is the exposure the single-name test misses.
Reconcile the stressed recoverable balances to Schedule F Part 3 before the results are used.
checklist.done: reserve deterioration and single- and two-name reinsurer default scenarios each produce a recomputed charge and surplus effect reconciled to Schedule F.

checklist.step: Run the liquidity stress test alongside the capital stresses
actions: Project the cash demand in each capital scenario: catastrophe claim payments over the first 90 days, surrender and withdrawal demand in the rate-rise and reputational scenarios, and collateral calls on derivatives.

Match the demand against the liquidity source ladder — cash, short-dated government holdings, repo capacity, committed facilities and Federal Home Loan Bank capacity — with a haircut and an access time on each source.
Identify the first day on which demand exceeds available liquidity in each scenario and state the shortfall in dollars.
Report any scenario producing a shortfall inside 30 days to the CFO and the Chief Risk Officer the same week, because a solvent insurer can still fail on liquidity.
checklist.done: each capital scenario has a paired liquidity projection with a source ladder, a first-shortfall day and a dollar shortfall, escalated where inside 30 days.

checklist.step: Run the reverse stress test to the point of capital failure
actions: Fix the end point as Total Adjusted Capital falling to the Company Action Level (200% of ACL) and, separately, to the Authorized Control Level.

Solve backwards for the combination of losses that would produce each end point, expressing it in business terms — for example a 1-in-X catastrophe alongside a stated equity fall and a stated reserve strengthening.
Assess how plausible each combination is and name the early indicators that would show it developing, handing them to the Enterprise Risk Manager for the monitoring pack.
Present the reverse stress test to the Board Risk Committee, since it is the scenario directors most reliably engage with.
checklist.done: the reverse stress test states, in business terms, the loss combination that reaches Company Action Level and Authorized Control Level, with named early indicators.

checklist.step: Translate every scenario result into a post-stress RBC position
actions: For each scenario, rebuild the affected RBC components on the stressed data and re-apply the covariance formula to produce a post-stress ACL.
Rebuild Total Adjusted Capital on the stressed surplus, including the AVR movement the scenario causes.
Compute the post-stress RBC ratio and the dollar distance to Company Action Level for every legal entity, not just the group.
Rank the scenarios by the ratio they produce so the binding scenario is unambiguous, and publish the ranking to the CFO and Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: every scenario has a post-stress ACL, TAC and RBC ratio per legal entity, and the scenarios are ranked to identify the binding one.

checklist.step: Assess the management actions that would be available in each scenario
actions: For each scenario breaching an internal trigger, list the levers and quantify the ratio recovery and the lead time for each — quota share, adverse development cover, asset de-risking, dividend suspension, parental contribution.
Test availability under the scenario's own conditions, since reinsurance capacity and capital markets are usually tightest exactly when the scenario bites.
Get written confirmation from the Reinsurance Manager on placeable capacity and from the CFO on any committed parental support before an action counts as available.
Record actions found to be unavailable, since removing an assumed action is itself a finding for the ORSA.
checklist.done: each breaching scenario has a costed action list with quantified recovery, lead time and written confirmation of availability under that scenario's conditions.

checklist.step: Validate the scenario models and archive every run
actions: Confirm every model used carries a current validation with no open high-severity finding before its results are released downstream.
Confirm each prescribed scenario file matches the regulator-published file byte for byte, and that no in-house adjustment was applied to it.
Register every run with its id, model version, input extract reference, scenario definition and result set, and lock the record.
Issue a validation note listing any result that must be presented with a caveat, and give it to the Chief Actuary before the results feed RBC or the ORSA.
checklist.done: every run is registered and locked with its model version and inputs, prescribed files are confirmed unmodified and a validation note names any caveated result.

checklist.step: Report the results to the board and feed them into RBC and the ORSA
actions: Build the reporting pack: scenario definitions, post-stress ratios per entity, the binding scenario, the liquidity shortfalls, the reverse stress test and the available management actions.
Present it to the Board Risk Committee and minute the committee's challenge and any request to re-run at a different severity.
Hand the C-3 and Rcat results to the Capital Model Actuary for the year-end RBC components in time for the February close lock and the March 1 filing.
Hand the stressed quantifications to the Chief Risk Officer for ORSA Section 2, quoting the archived run ids so the ORSA cites reproducible figures.
checklist.done: the board pack is presented and minuted, and the C-3, Rcat and ORSA Section 2 figures are handed over quoting archived run ids ahead of their deadlines.

checklist.step: Prepare the asset adequacy and AG 53 supporting documentation
actions: Run asset adequacy analysis under VM-30 on the reconciled base and form the opinion that supports the statutory Actuarial Opinion filed with the March 1 annual statement.

Where the entity holds projected high net yield assets in scope of Actuarial Guideline 53, prepare the AG 53 supporting documentation on the asset assumptions, the reinvestment assumptions and the sensitivity results.
File the AG 53 documentation with the domiciliary commissioner by April 1 and record the transmission and receipt.
Cross-check that the scenarios used for asset adequacy are consistent with the library used for RBC and the ORSA, and explain any deliberate difference in the memorandum.
checklist.done: the asset adequacy opinion supports the March 1 Actuarial Opinion, AG 53 documentation is filed by April 1 with a receipt, and any scenario difference is explained in the memorandum.

testing.step: Build the population of scenarios and runs for the cycle
actions: Extract every run registered in the model governance repository for the cycle with its scenario, entity, model version, input extract reference and result set.
Compare the run list to the Board Risk Committee-approved scenario library and list every approved scenario with no registered run as an automatic exception.
Add every scenario result quoted in the RBC components, the board pack and ORSA Section 2 as separate population rows so downstream use is testable.
testing.done: the population covers every approved scenario, every registered run and every downstream use, with unrun approved scenarios already flagged.

testing.step: Reconcile the scenario inputs to the statutory source of record
actions: Agree the liability extract used for the cycle to Exhibit 5 or Schedule P and the asset extract to Schedule D and Schedule BA as at the data cut date.
Confirm every run in the population cites the same reconciled extract, since a run on a private data pull cannot be relied on downstream.
Quantify any unreconciled amount as a percentage of the exposure base and list anything above 1% as a fail.
Confirm the catastrophe exposure set ties to the policy administration in-force count and total insured value within 2%.
testing.done: all runs cite the one reconciled extract, statutory reconciliation is within 1% of the exposure base and cat exposure ties to in-force within 2%.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of runs
actions: Take 100% of prescribed regulatory scenarios (C-3 Phase I, C-3 Phase II and the Rcat return periods) and 100% of the binding scenario and the reverse stress test.
Take 6 further runs at random using a recorded seed, spread across asset, insurance, reinsurance and liquidity scenarios, for a minimum of 15 runs.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
Add every prior-cycle exception run as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers all prescribed scenarios, the binding scenario and the reverse stress test, is reproducible from the seed and carries forward prior exceptions.

testing.step: Verify the prescribed scenario files were run unmodified
actions: Download the regulator-published scenario file for the reporting year and compare it byte for byte to the file archived against the run.
Inspect the run configuration for any scenario weight, path adjustment or scenario-count reduction applied inside the model.
Confirm the scenario count and confidence level used for C-3 Phase II match the instructions rather than a reduced count adopted for runtime.
Any modification, omission or reduction is a fail regardless of its effect on the answer, because the instruction prescribes the input.
testing.done: each prescribed scenario file matches the published file byte for byte and no path, weight or count adjustment was applied.

testing.step: Re-execute a sample of runs and compare to the recorded results
actions: Restore the archived model version and input extract for each sampled run and re-execute it without opening the recorded result first.
Compare the re-executed result to the recorded result and require an explanation for any difference over 1% of the scenario's surplus effect.
Confirm the model version restored is the one the run record names; a result produced on a version later patched is not reproducible evidence.
Capture the re-execution log and the comparison into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled run is re-executed on its archived version and inputs, with every difference over 1% of the surplus effect explained.

testing.step: Re-perform the catastrophe net loss derivation
actions: Take the gross exceedance probability curve from the archived cat run and independently apply the in-force reinsurance structure from the treaty documents held by the Reinsurance Manager.
Recompute net loss at the 1-in-100 and 1-in-250 return periods, including reinstatement premium and the effect of any exhausted layer.
Compare your net figures to those entered on the Rcat pages and to those used in the board pack, since the two are often derived at different times.
Confirm the multi-event year scenario reflects the reinstatement limits actually purchased rather than unlimited reinstatement.
testing.done: net PML at each required return period is independently derived from the gross curve and the treaty terms and agrees with the Rcat pages and the board pack.

testing.step: Trace scenario results through to RBC, the ORSA and the board pack
actions: For each sampled run, find where its result was used — the C-3 or Rcat RBC line, the ORSA Section 2 stressed quantification, the board reporting pack — and confirm the figure matches the archived result set.
Confirm the ORSA and the board pack cite the archived run id, so a reviewer can be pointed straight at the run.
Investigate any downstream figure that cannot be traced to a registered run; an untraceable figure in a filed document is the most serious finding available here.
Confirm any caveat the validation note required was actually carried into the downstream document.
testing.done: every sampled result traces to its downstream use with matching figures and a cited run id, and required caveats appear in the downstream documents.

testing.step: Recompute the post-stress ratios and the reverse stress test point
actions: Rebuild post-stress ACL for three sampled scenarios by re-applying the covariance formula to the stressed components, and rebuild TAC on the stressed surplus including the AVR movement.
Recompute the post-stress RBC ratio and the dollar distance to Company Action Level per legal entity and compare to the reported figures.
Independently solve the reverse stress test back from 200% of ACL and compare the loss combination to the one reported.
Confirm the scenario ranking is correct, since a mis-ranked set means the wrong scenario was treated as binding by the board.
testing.done: post-stress ACL, TAC, ratios and the reverse stress test point are independently recomputed and the reported scenario ranking is confirmed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a finding per exception carrying the scenario, entity, run id and whether the failure was prescribed-scenario integrity, input reconciliation, reproducibility, downstream trace or calibration.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — scenario file modified, run on a private extract, model patched after the run, result quoted without a run id, severity not re-calibrated after a real event exceeded it — and name an owner.
Where a prescribed scenario was altered or an RBC component rests on an unreproducible run, notify the Chief Actuary and assess whether an amended RBC report is owed.
Carry every open finding into the next cycle's scenario approval as a mandatory pre-condition.
testing.done: every exception has a finding, a failure type, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a next-cycle pre-condition.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the reproducibility rate across re-executed runs and the prescribed-scenario integrity rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing workpaper references and stating whether the C-3, Rcat and ORSA Section 2 figures rest on reproducible runs.
Have the independent reviewer, who built, calibrated and executed no scenario in the cycle and sits outside Actuarial and Capital Management, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Board Risk Committee and the Audit Committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper under Risk/StressTesting/<cycle year>.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the reproducibility rate, prescribed-scenario integrity rate and a conclusion exists in the repository with a committee reporting date.
